# Puzzle prefabs

<!-- Generated by pnpm content:docs from src/content/data/prefab; do not edit. -->

A prefab is a kit piece for puzzle designers (mw-e15.4): 18 named bundles of
spawns, built only from existing world components (doors, plates, optics, light sources, push
rules, liquid volumes), with a small signal graph where the piece has behaviour of its own. They
are data, never code: a prefab may not introduce a component. A missing general property goes to
the e03 systemic layer first.

Place one in a scene file under `prefabs`:

```json
{ "id": "mirror-1", "prefab": "rotatable-mirror", "at": [-6, 0, 5], "yaw": 90, "params": { "stepAngle": 45 } }
```

The loader expands the instance into plain spawns `mirror-1-<name>` and, for a prefab with a graph,
a signal graph `mirror-1`, before the sim, the checks or the puzzle runtime see the scene. `yaw`
(0, 90, 180, 270) turns the whole instance, its positions and its directions. A parameter left
out takes its default; one with no default is required, and an instance without it fails to load
naming it. Outputs marked "signal" are read by puzzle goals and signal graphs as
`<instance>/<node>`; "entity" outputs are the spawn itself. Every prefab stands in the demo scene
`prefab-gallery` (`?scene=prefab-gallery`).

## Beam sensor (`beam-sensor`)

A light receiver that turns on once a beam at or above its threshold has been held on it for the dwell time, and off when the light goes. Half a metre up, at the height of the mirror and lens stands.

Tags: `light`. Built from: `lightReceiver`.

Spawns (each named `<instance>-<name>`): `receiver`.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Range | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `threshold` | number | `0.5` | 0.05–10 | Intensity at or above which light counts. |
| `dwellSeconds` | number | `0.5` | 0–30 s | Seconds the light must be held before it turns on. |
| `mode` | enum | `momentary` | one of `momentary`, `latching` | momentary goes off with the light; latching until reset. |

| Input | On spawn | What drives it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `beam` | `receiver` | A light beam reaching the sensor. |

| Output | Read as | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `lit` | signal `<instance>/lit` | On while enough light has been held on the sensor. |

## Beam source (`beam-source`)

A light emitter casting a beam along the instance's facing (north at yaw 0), half a metre up so it meets the mirror and lens stands. Turn the instance to aim it.

Tags: `light`. Built from: `beamEmitter`.

Spawns (each named `<instance>-<name>`): `emitter`.

## Bell (`bell`)

A bell that rings when struck from afar by an arrow, a thrown object or a spell, and stays on for a few seconds, loud enough to carry. Wire its output to a door or let a puzzle listen for it.

Tags: `sound`. Built from: `impactSwitch`.

Spawns (each named `<instance>-<name>`): `bell`.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Range | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mode` | enum | `momentary` | one of `momentary`, `latching` | momentary stays on for the hold time; latching until reset. |
| `holdSeconds` | number | `3` | 0–60 s | Momentary: seconds it stays on after a strike. |

| Input | On spawn | What drives it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `strike` | `bell` | Any impact above its energy: arrow, thrown crate, spell. |

| Output | Read as | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `rung` | signal `<instance>/rung` | On while the bell has been struck (for its hold time, or until reset). |

## Bell sequence (`bell-sequence`)

Three bells, low, mid and high, that must be struck in the order the instance expects (low, high, mid by default): the answering half of a bell-tower puzzle. A wrong bell starts the sequence over and rings a wrong chime; the right order rings a bright chime and latches solved until reset. Each bell is struck as the single bell prefab is: an arrow, a thrown object or a spell.

Tags: `sound`, `sequence`. Built from: `impactSwitch`.

Spawns (each named `<instance>-<name>`): `bell-low`, `bell-mid`, `bell-high`.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Range | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `first` | enum | `low` | one of `low`, `mid`, `high` | The bell to strike first. |
| `second` | enum | `high` | one of `low`, `mid`, `high` | The bell to strike second. |
| `third` | enum | `mid` | one of `low`, `mid`, `high` | The bell to strike third. |
| `holdSeconds` | number | `1` | 0–60 s | Seconds a bell stays on after a strike. |

| Input | On spawn | What drives it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `strike` | `bell-low` | Any impact above a bell's energy: arrow, thrown crate, spell. The low bell is the first spawn. |

| Output | Read as | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `solved` | signal `<instance>/solved` | On once the bells have been struck in the expected order. |

## Brazier (`brazier`)

A brazier that burns, can be put out by water or wind and is relit by any heat, with a fire sensor so the puzzle can ask whether it burns. It is a light source: its light and heat are the world's, not the prefab's.

Tags: `fire`, `light`. Built from: `lightSource`.

Spawns (each named `<instance>-<name>`): `brazier`.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Range | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `unlit` | boolean | `true` | true or false | Starts dark (heat lights it). |

| Input | On spawn | What drives it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `heat` | `brazier` | Any heat stimulus lights it; water or wind puts it out. |

| Output | Read as | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `lit` | signal `<instance>/lit` | On while the brazier burns. |

## Counterweight lift (`counterweight-lift`)

A lift gate raised by a counterweight: put enough weight on the plate (a crate, a statue, a companion) and the gate rises; take it off and the gate falls. The plate's window is the counterweight, so too little keeps it shut and, with a ceiling, too much does too.

Tags: `weight`. Built from: `door`, `plate`.

Spawns (each named `<instance>-<name>`): `plate`, `lift`.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Range | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `counterweight` | number | `30` | 1–1000 kg | Weight on the plate that raises the lift. |

| Input | On spawn | What drives it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `weight` | `plate` | Anything resting on the plate counts by its weight. |

| Output | Read as | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `raised` | signal `<instance>/raised` | On while the lift gate is raised. |

## Plate timed door (`plate-timed-door`)

A door held open by a pressure plate and for a while after it is released: the race-the-door puzzle. Step on the plate (or weigh it with a crate) and the door opens; once the plate is clear the door stays open for the window, then shuts. The door is moved only by the signal, never by hand.

Tags: `time`, `weight`. Built from: `door`, `plate`.

Spawns (each named `<instance>-<name>`): `door`, `plate`.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Range | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `profile` | enum | `sliding-door` | one of `sliding-door`, `portcullis` | What kind of door. |
| `windowSeconds` | number | `8` | 0.5–120 s | Seconds the door stays open after the plate is released. |
| `minWeight` | number | `25` | 1–500 kg | Weight that presses the plate. |

| Input | On spawn | What drives it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `plate` | `plate` | Weight on the plate; stepping on it again during the window keeps the door open until it is released. |

| Output | Read as | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `open` | signal `<instance>/open` | On while the plate is held and for the window after it is released. |

## Rotatable mirror (`rotatable-mirror`)

A mirror on a stand that bounces light beams and turns in steps with Interact. Its face points along the instance's facing at yaw 0 (south, towards a beam travelling north). Wire a beam source, one or more of these and a beam sensor for the classic light puzzle.

## Rotatable statue (`rotatable-statue`)

A heavy stone statue the player turns in fixed steps with Interact (and can drag). Placed at yaw 0 it faces north; a quarter turn of the instance turns it east, south, west. A facing sensor per compass direction tells the puzzle which way it looks: a statue that must face the sunrise, a row of statues that must all look at the door.

Tags: `weight`, `facing`. Built from: `push`.

Spawns (each named `<instance>-<name>`): `statue`.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Range | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stepAngle` | number | `90` | 15–180 degrees | Degrees one turn rotates it; 90 gives the four compass facings. |

| Input | On spawn | What drives it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `turn` | `statue` | Interact with the statue turns it by one step; a rotate spell or a shove with a rotate effect does the same. |

| Output | Read as | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `facing-north` | signal `<instance>/facing-north` | On while the statue faces north (+z). |
| `facing-east` | signal `<instance>/facing-east` | On while the statue faces east (+x). |
| `facing-south` | signal `<instance>/facing-south` | On while the statue faces south (-z). |
| `facing-west` | signal `<instance>/facing-west` | On while the statue faces west (-x). |

## Scale plate pair (`scale-plate-pair`)

Two pressure plates side by side, each with a weight window; the pair is balanced when both are in their window together. Put a 20 kg crate on each, or one 40 kg crate and a friend: the puzzle only asks for weight.

Tags: `weight`. Built from: `plate`.

Spawns (each named `<instance>-<name>`): `left`, `right`.

## Sound clue (`sound-clue`)

A hidden chime source that plays three chimes in order, one second apart (by default), when its button is pressed: the listening half of a bell-tower puzzle. Put the source behind a wall and the button where the player can reach it; the chimes come from the source, so they are muffled and panned by the audio engine, and with sound captions on each shows as text with its direction, for example [High chime, left].

Tags: `sound`, `sequence`. Built from: `switch`.

Spawns (each named `<instance>-<name>`): `source`, `listen`.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Range | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `first` | enum | `chime-low` | one of `chime-low`, `chime-mid`, `chime-high` | The first chime. |
| `second` | enum | `chime-high` | one of `chime-low`, `chime-mid`, `chime-high` | The second chime. |
| `third` | enum | `chime-mid` | one of `chime-low`, `chime-mid`, `chime-high` | The third chime. |
| `spacing` | number | `1` | 0.2–10 s | Seconds between one chime and the next. |

| Input | On spawn | What drives it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `listen` | `listen` | The button; pressing it while the chimes play does nothing. |

| Output | Read as | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `playing` | signal `<instance>/chimes` | On from the press until the last chime has sounded. |

## Water basin (`water-basin`)

A stone basin of water with a drain, a valve to open it and a pressure plate on the floor of the basin. Turn the valve and the water runs out; once the level is below the plate the plate can be reached and weighted. The valve is a lever, so Mage Hand works from across the room.

Tags: `water`, `weight`. Built from: `liquid`, `plate`, `switch`.

Spawns (each named `<instance>-<name>`): `basin`, `plate`, `valve`.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Range | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

| `depth` | number | `0.8` | 0.1–3 m | How deep the water stands at the start (not above the brim). |
| `drainRate` | number | `0.1` | 0.01–2 m/s | How fast the level falls while the valve is open. |
| `plateWeight` | number | `10` | 1–500 kg | Weight that turns the floor plate on. |

| Output | Read as | Meaning |

| `plate-pressed` | signal `<instance>/plate-pressed` | On while enough weight rests on the basin-floor plate. |

## Weighted crate set (`weighted-crate-set`)

Four identical-looking crates of 5, 10, 20 and 40 kg in a row along x, the weights the plate puzzles are tuned against. A crate is pushable and carryable; its weight is the world property `weight`, so a plate counts it like anything else.
